message.content:
You're prepping backlog-refinement notes for a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann) FED Lead, for Jira ticket SFCC-801 "global/country-currency-selector — PWA Component". Read-only research — you are not writing to Jira or Confluence.

I've already done first-pass research on this one, verified live today (2026-09-03). Your job is to fill the remaining gaps (comments, exact AC, any Figma attachment) and produce the final structured brief, NOT to re-derive what's below.

CONFIRMED GROUND TRUTH:
- Status: "Blocked" (the ticket itself is flagged blocked in Jira, not just "To Do"). Parent epic: SFCC-2 "PWA Kit Components".
- Description: a right-anchored slide-in drawer, accepts props to control which optional sections render (country/currency/language). Does NOT own redirect logic — that's covered by SFCC-688 or SFCC-817.
- Related tickets (via issuelinks): SFCC-688 "Regional Storefronts — Country & Language Selector" (status: Ready For Review) — the shopper-experience Level-2 story this component feeds. SFCC-736 "pdp/drawer" (status: Ready for QA, already merged as PR #67) — check whether its shell is reusable here. SFCC-49 "Country List Configuration" (status: Tech design) — a backend config dependency, plausibly the actual reason this ticket is Blocked.
- DUPLICATION RISK, LIVE AND UNRESOLVED: SFCC-467 "global/country-currency-selector — local pricing" (status: To Do) describes an almost identical component ("country/currency selector UI component... allowing shoppers to indicate their shipping country... prices update to configured currency") but has ZERO issuelinks connecting it to this ticket or to SFCC-688. This exact duplication risk was first flagged 2026-08-11 (three tickets covering similar ground: SFCC-79, SFCC-467, SFCC-688) and is STILL unreconciled three weeks later. SFCC-467 also references a DIFFERENT dependency ticket — SFCC-44 ("country-currency mapping") — vs. this ticket's SFCC-49 ("Country List Configuration"). There may be two parallel, unreconciled backend config tickets too.
- DESIGN GAP: Figma 04.7 Component Inventory (re-checked live today, unchanged since 2026-08-10) shows "Drawer" as "Designs Empty"/"Incomplete" — this ticket's own description depends on that same shared drawer shell. No "country-currency-selector" row exists in that tracker at all.
- CROSS-STORY PATTERN: SFCC-831 (country-language-mismatch) and SFCC-315 (Cart Drawer) ALSO depend on this same generic Drawer shell.
- Today is 2026-09-03, real Sprint 4 runs 2026-08-24–2026-09-07 (active), Sprint 5 runs 2026-09-07–2026-09-21. .docs/memory/sprintScope.md is confirmed stale — don't cite it.

DO THIS:
1. Fetch the full ticket with comments: jira_get_issue(issue_key='SFCC-801', fields='summary,description,status,issuelinks,comment,attachment,parent', comment_limit=20). Look specifically for any comment already addressing the SFCC-467 duplication or explaining why this ticket is Blocked.
2. Fetch SFCC-49 and SFCC-467 (jira_get_issue, description+status is enough for both) to characterize the actual blocking dependency and the duplication risk precisely.
3. Apply the seven-point sizing lens: (1) any FE impact? (2) is the requirement clear enough to size? (3) which surfaces does it touch? (4) design/Figma dependencies — confirm the Drawer gap? (5) API/backend dependencies — name SFCC-49 (or SFCC-44 if that turns out to be the real one) as the likely reason for Blocked status? (6) pure FE, shared FE/BE, or needs architecture input? (7) size now, or need clarification first?
4. Read for the four standing axes: behaviour, desktop/mobile, a11y, data (country list source, currency formatting per locale) — flag anything genuinely unclear.
5. Altitude: BAs own component-decomposition questions, devs own atomic/build questions.

OUTPUT, in this exact shape:
- One-line plain-language summary
- Seven lens answers
- Four axes, flagging what's unclear
- Design status + source (state the Drawer-Incomplete finding plainly)
- Why the ticket is Blocked — name the specific dependency you found
- The SFCC-467 duplication flag as a top-line item — recommend who should reconcile it (likely Jasmijn Tsang as story author, or Izzy as the one operationally driving the component-story framework — use whichever the ticket data actually supports)
- Specific questions to raise, each tagged with who should answer it
- One-line readiness call

1	/**
2	 * Zimmermann country configuration — combines SCAPI-derived site/locale/
3	 * currency truth (countries.generated.ts, regenerate via
4	 * `npm run sync:regional-config`) with a hand-maintained overlay for the
5	 * fields Business Manager/SCAPI has no concept of: shipping country,
6	 * checkout ownership, and boutique region grouping.
7	 *
8	 * Used by: URL routing, IP-detection prompt, checkout redirect logic,
9	 * boutique location filtering, hreflang generation.
10	 *
11	 * When adding a country:
12	 *   1. Add it to config/sites.overlay.js (and e2e/fixtures/site.overlay.js
13	 *      if it needs e2e coverage), then run `npm run sync:regional-config`.
14	 *   2. Add its business-logic overlay entry below (shippingCountry,
15	 *      checkoutOwner, globalEPricing, boutiqueRegion).
16	 *   3. Ensure a compiled translation exists in overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/.
17	 *
18	 * Unresolved — do not hard-code:
19	 *   - NZ/Oceania currency routing
20	 *   - Denmark routing
21	 *   - China
22	 */
23	
24	import { GENERATED_COUNTRIES } from './countries.generated';
25	
26	/**
27	 * Who owns checkout for this site's domestic path.
28	 * For HK and ME, Global-e always owns checkout AND pricing from PDP onward.
29	 * For AU, US, GB, EU: SFCC owns domestic paths; Global-e takes over when the
30	 * user's shipping destination is outside the site's domestic market.
31	 */
32	export type CheckoutOwner = 'sfcc' | 'global-e' | 'hybrid';
33	
34	export type CountryConfig = {
35	  /** URL path segment, e.g. 'au', 'us', 'fr-eu' */
36	  urlSlug: string;
37	  /** The real SFCC site this locale routes to */
38	  sfccSiteId: string;
39	  /** IETF locale used by PWA Kit / SFCC, e.g. 'en-AU' */
40	  locale: string;
41	  /** ISO 4217 currency code */
42	  currency: string;
43	  /** ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 shipping/tax country */
44	  shippingCountry: string;
45	  /**
46	   * Checkout owner for this site's domestic path.
47	   * Branch checkout AND pricing logic from this field at PDP/cart level —
48	   * not only at the checkout page.
49	   */
50	  checkoutOwner: CheckoutOwner;
51	  /**
52	   * When true, Global-e owns pricing, currency, and tax display from PDP
53	   * onward — do not render SFCC prices on these paths.
54	   */
55	  globalEPricing: boolean;
56	  /** Key used to filter boutique locations for this region */
57	  boutiqueRegion: string;
58	};
59	
60	type CountryOverlayEntry = Pick<
61	  CountryConfig,
62	  'shippingCountry' | 'checkoutOwner' | 'globalEPricing' | 'boutiqueRegion'
63	>;
64	
65	/**
66	 * Hand-maintained business/geo data, keyed the same way as
67	 * countries.generated.ts (URL slug; 'au' for the root/default site).
68	 *
69	 * 'en-ca' (US international) is defined here ready to go, but has no
70	 * matching entry in countries.generated.ts yet — it's excluded from the
71	 * final COUNTRIES export below until the ZimmermannUSIntl site is added to
72	 * config/sites.overlay.js (pending BM confirmation of the real site ID —
73	 * see .docs/planning/regionalConfigSyncPlan.md).
74	 */
75	const COUNTRY_OVERLAY: Record<string, CountryOverlayEntry> = {
76	  au: { shippingCountry: 'AU', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'australia' },
77	  us: { shippingCountry: 'US', checkoutOwner: 'hybrid', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'usa' },
78	  'en-ca': { shippingCountry: 'CA', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'usa' }, // TBC — pending ZimmermannUSIntl
79	  uk: { shippingCountry: 'GB', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'uk' },
80	  'en-eu': { shippingCountry: 'DE', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; shipping country resolved at checkout
81	  'fr-eu': { shippingCountry: 'FR', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' },
82	  'it-eu': { shippingCountry: 'IT', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; shipping country resolved at checkout
83	  'es-eu': { shippingCountry: 'ES', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; shipping country resolved at checkout
84	  'en-ch': { shippingCountry: 'CH', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; Global-e resolves shipping country
85	  hk: { shippingCountry: 'HK', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'hong-kong' },
86	  'en-ae': { shippingCountry: 'AE', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'middle-east' },
87	};
88	
89	/**
90	 * Keyed by urlSlug for O(1) lookup in routing/middleware.
91	 * AU is the exception: it has no URL prefix (root domain). Its key is 'au'
92	 * but urlSlug is '' — routing falls back to DEFAULT_COUNTRY_SLUG when no
93	 * prefix is detected.
94	 */
95	// Fail loud, not silent, if BM/the sync script produced a slug with no
96	// matching business-logic overlay — that means someone added a site to
97	// config/sites.overlay.js and ran `npm run sync:regional-config` without
98	// adding the corresponding COUNTRY_OVERLAY entry above. The reverse case
99	// (an overlay entry with no generated data yet, e.g. 'en-ca' pending the
100	// US-split site ID) is intentional and handled by the filter below instead.
101	const missingOverlays = Object.keys(GENERATED_COUNTRIES).filter((slug) => !(slug in COUNTRY_OVERLAY));
102	if (missingOverlays.length) {
103	  throw new Error(
104	    `countries.ts: config/sites.overlay.js has a site for slug(s) '${missingOverlays.join(', ')}' with no ` +
105	      `matching COUNTRY_OVERLAY entry — add shippingCountry/checkoutOwner/globalEPricing/boutiqueRegion for it.`,
106	  );
107	}
108	
109	export const COUNTRIES: Record<string, CountryConfig> = Object.fromEntries(
110	  Object.entries(COUNTRY_OVERLAY)
111	    .filter(([slug]) => slug in GENERATED_COUNTRIES)
112	    .map(([slug, overlay]) => [
113	      slug,
114	      {
115	        urlSlug: slug === 'au' ? '' : slug,
116	        ...(GENERATED_COUNTRIES as Record<string, { sfccSiteId: string; locale: string; currency: string }>)[slug],
117	        ...overlay,
118	      },
119	    ]),
120	);
121	
122	/** Fallback when no URL slug is present or IP detection fails. */
123	export const DEFAULT_COUNTRY_SLUG = 'au';
124	
125	/** Lookup by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code — used by IP-detection prompt. */
126	export const COUNTRY_BY_SHIPPING_CODE: Record<string, CountryConfig> = Object.fromEntries(
127	  Object.values(COUNTRIES).map((c) => [c.shippingCountry, c]),
128	);

Here is the completed backlog-refinement brief for SFCC-801, with all gaps filled from a fresh live Jira pull (today, 2026-09-03) plus a codebase check that materially sharpens two of your open questions.

---

## SFCC-801 — global/country-currency-selector — PWA Component

**One-line summary:** A reusable, right-anchored slide-in drawer that lets a shopper pick country/currency/language (redirect logic lives elsewhere) — the drawer *mechanics* already exist and are merged, but the component's own design, its exact AC, and its real dependency set are all still unresolved, and it silently overlaps with another backlog item (SFCC-467).

### Seven-point sizing lens

1. **FE impact?** Yes — 100% FE ticket, a new React/Chakra component under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`, parented to Epic SFCC-2 "PWA Kit Components."
2. **Requirement clear enough to size?** Partially. The shell shape (right-anchored drawer, prop-gated sections) is unambiguous and de-risked by precedent (see Design status below), but there is **no Acceptance Criteria list at all** — the description is a single user-story paragraph, nothing else — plus the SFCC-467 overlap and the missing design content. Not confidently sizeable yet; a rough T-shirt estimate for "shell reuse only" is plausible.
3. **Which surfaces?** Global — every regional storefront (`global/` prefix). Trigger point is never stated in SFCC-801 itself; only the sibling SFCC-467 guesses "likely component placement in the header" (Header/Nav epic cross-dependency). It shares its underlying shell with at least 3 other known consumers: SFCC-736 (PDP drawer, shipped), SFCC-315 (Cart Drawer), SFCC-831 (country-language-mismatch).
4. **Design/Figma dependencies?** Confirmed gap — see Design status section below.
5. **API/backend dependencies?** SFCC-49 "Country List Configuration" (Tech design) is the one formally linked dependency — see Blocked-reason section, which sharpens this further than a flat "waiting on SFCC-49."
6. **Pure FE / shared FE-BE / architecture input?** Shared FE/BE at the data layer, pure FE and already-precedented at the component-architecture layer (nothing new to design architecturally — it's a new consumer of an existing pattern, same shape as `zimmPdpDrawer`).
7. **Size now or clarify first?** Clarify first. Cannot responsibly size against: no AC, no attached design, an unreconciled duplicate story, and an imprecisely-scoped backend dependency (below).

### Four standing axes

- **Behaviour:** Unclear. The description explicitly excludes redirect logic ("SFCC-688 or SFCC-817") but doesn't say which of those two the drawer's own confirm/apply action actually triggers, or whether both are in play. Worth noting: SFCC-688 and SFCC-817 turn out to be two *different* redirect flavours (SFCC-688 = user-triggered selector redirect, status Ready For Review; SFCC-817 = automatic first-visit IP-geolocation redirect + AU gating, status **In Refinement**) — the "or" in SFCC-801's description likely reflects that these are genuinely two separate mechanisms, not an actual open decision, but SFCC-801 doesn't say which applies to its own confirm action. Flag as unclear.
- **Desktop/mobile:** Better-covered than expected — the reusable `ZimmDrawer` atom (see below) already ships `large`/`small`/`mobile` size variants with a proven tablet-breakpoint collapse, exercised today by `zimmPdpDrawer`. What's still unclear is this component's own *content* layout at each size (list density, section ordering) — no design exists for that yet.
- **A11y:** Foundation is solid and already built: `ZimmDrawer` gets Chakra's focus trap, initial focus, focus restore, body-scroll lock, and Escape/overlay-click-to-close for free (confirmed in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/index.tsx`). Unclear: the interaction pattern for the actual country/currency/language lists themselves — radio-group/listbox with arrow-key navigation, or a flat list of buttons? Not specified anywhere.
- **Data:** More nuanced than "nothing exists yet." A live country→currency→locale→shippingCountry mapping **already exists in code**: `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` (Tier 1, SCAPI-sourced via `countries.generated.ts` + a hand-maintained overlay), exposed via `useCountryConfig()`. It currently covers AU/US/en-ca/UK/three EU variants/HK/en-ae — but its own header comment explicitly flags **NZ/Oceania currency routing, Denmark routing, and China as unresolved, do-not-hard-code**. So the real data gap is finishing global coverage, not building from zero. Separately, SFCC-801 is linked only to SFCC-49 (country→**storefront-routing** mapping), not to SFCC-44 (country→**currency** mapping, referenced only by the unlinked SFCC-467) — despite SFCC-801's own scope including a currency section. Currency *formatting* has precedent only inside PDP-specific files (`productInfo.ts`, `staticProductHeader.tsx`), not a shared utility — flag as unclear whether this ticket owns extracting one.

### Design status

Confirmed gap, from three independent angles: (1) Figma 04.7 Component Inventory still shows "Drawer" as Designs Empty/Incomplete with no "country-currency-selector" row at all; (2) the live ticket pull today returned **zero attachments** on SFCC-801; (3) a teammate is chasing this the same day — see Blocked-reason below. However, this gap is narrower than it looks: the drawer *shell mechanics* (slide-in, overlay, sizing, close button, focus handling) are already fully designed-and-built, merged to `develop` via PR #67 (SFCC-736). `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/index.tsx`'s own doc comment states it owns "the close button only — no header/tab content of its own, so both a tabbed header (ZimmPdpDrawer) and a plain-title header (**e.g. a future country/currency selector**) can compose on top of it" — i.e., this exact ticket was anticipated when the shell was built. The real remaining design gap is scoped specifically to this component's *own content* (country/currency/language section layouts), not the drawer mechanism.

### Why the ticket is Blocked

The only formally issue-linked dependency is **SFCC-49 "Country List Configuration"** (status: Tech design) — its own description calls it "a foundation for all downstream storefront routing and navigation stories," which fits. But two things sharpen this beyond a flat "waiting on SFCC-49":
- SFCC-49 is scoped to country→**storefront-routing** mapping, not currency. SFCC-801's own currency section more precisely depends on SFCC-44 ("country-currency mapping and maintenance") — which isn't linked to SFCC-801 at all, only referenced by the probable-duplicate SFCC-467.
- In practice, the missing **design** is at least as live a blocker right now: Hazel Marie Cacalda's comment today (2026-09-03, same day as this research) directly asks Jasmijn Tsang and Kiera Rikard-Bell to "add the final approved design for this component" — unanswered as of this pull. Neither of the two comments on this ticket states a reason for the Blocked status or references SFCC-467 — the Blocked reason is inferred from linked-ticket state, not asserted by anyone in-thread.

### SFCC-467 duplication — top-line flag

Still live and unreconciled, reconfirmed today: SFCC-467 "global/country-currency-selector — local pricing" (To Do) describes materially the same UI component with zero issuelinks to SFCC-801 or SFCC-688, and depends on a *different* backend ticket (SFCC-44) than the one SFCC-801 links (SFCC-49).

**Recommend Jasmijn Tsang reconcile this** — the ticket data supports her specifically, not Izzy (who has no footprint anywhere in this ticket's data): Jasmijn is SFCC-467's own reporter, **and** she's independently and directly tagged on SFCC-801 twice already — once by Emma Kirwan ("this ticket is approved," 2026-09-01) and once by Hazel today chasing the design. She's already the connective thread between both tickets without anyone having named the duplication itself to her yet.

### Questions to raise

- **[BA — Jasmijn Tsang]** Are SFCC-801 and SFCC-467 the same component under two tickets, or genuinely distinct (SFCC-801 = shell/props, SFCC-467 = the price-update behaviour on selection)? If distinct, SFCC-801 should explicitly exclude price-update logic the same way it already excludes redirect logic, naming SFCC-467 as owner.
- **[BA — Jasmijn Tsang / Kiera Rikard-Bell, per Hazel's own comment]** Where does the "final approved design" actually live, and can it be attached to SFCC-801 and added as a row in the 04.7 tracker?
- **[BA]** Should SFCC-801 name explicitly which redirect flow its own confirm/apply action feeds — SFCC-688's user-triggered redirect, SFCC-817's automatic IP-geolocation redirect, or both — instead of the current "or" phrasing?
- **[BA]** Should SFCC-801 add an explicit dependency link to SFCC-44 (currency mapping) alongside SFCC-49 (routing mapping), given its own scope includes a currency section?
- **[BA]** Write actual Acceptance Criteria — none exist today beyond the narrative story.
- **[Dev]** Confirm `overrides/app/config/countries.ts`/`useCountryConfig()` is the intended data source, and whether SFCC-801 can ship against its already-covered markets (AU/US/en-ca/UK/EU variants/HK/en-ae) while NZ/Oceania/Denmark/China land in a follow-up once SFCC-49 completes.
- **[Dev]** Confirm the interaction pattern for the country/currency/language lists (listbox/radio-group vs. plain buttons) for a11y implementation.

### Readiness call

Not ready to size or pull — hold in refinement pending the design attachment, the SFCC-467 reconciliation, and an explicit AC list; the underlying drawer shell is no longer a risk (already built and merged), so once those three unblock, this should size quickly.
